brief: Tonight is Pull B, and you come into it off two full days of rest — you last trained Monday. That changes the card from the one you would have seen Tuesday. The bent-over row is back to all four sets: Tuesday it was cut to three because it would have been your sixth training day in a row, and you have since taken the rest, so that reason is gone. Start at 120, then 140, 145, and 150 for ten. The 120 and 140 are the real raises — you finished ten reps on 115, 135 and 145 last Pull B, so those two openers had gone stale. 145 stays put on purpose, because the one rep you still owe on this lift is the tenth at 150, and making the warm-up sets heavier is exactly what would cost you it. Close-grip pulldown goes up: you took 120 for a clean ten on all three sets, and 127.5 is the smallest step this machine has. Straight-arm pulldown, shrugs and incline curls all stay at the same weight, because on each one the next notch up is a jump of about twenty percent and your log has not paid for it yet — chase the extra reps instead and the weight is yours next time. Cable reverse curl comes down to 35. At 37.5 your reps went 12, 11, 10 and the last two were under the twelve this slot asks for, which means the weight is wrong, not your effort. On the day: rest a full three minutes on the row and about seventy-five seconds on everything after the pulldown. Your conditioning is still the thin part of this prep — one cardio session in the last two weeks and one bodyweight reading on file. Getting on a bike for twenty easy minutes tomorrow, and stepping on a scale, would both do more for March than any weight on tonight's card.

dissent.progression: 37.5 is going backwards, so drop to 35 — the nearest loadable step down — and run three sets of twelve.
dissent.recovery: Genuinely too heavy and getting worse; drop to 34 for three sets of twelve.
dissent.why: Both seats want the same thing and only the number differs, so this came down to which number exists. I checked the machine rather than taking either seat's word: the gear record for the dual cable stack resolves the add-on weights to 1.25 and 2.5 per handle, so the ladder below 37.5 runs 32.5, 33.75, 35. There is no 34 — the app would have silently snapped it and put a weight on the card that no trainer argued for. Progression's 35 is a real pin plus a real add-on, and it is the smaller retreat of the two, which is what a lift failing by one or two reps deserves.

proposals.why: Still waiting on your answer from Tuesday: Push A holds the only face pulls left in your week, the ones you wrote "Do you have a brain?" next to on 31 July, and this puts the reverse pec deck there instead — same back of the shoulder, and it is the machine you have carried from 82.5 to 90 without missing a set.

Still waiting on your answer from Tuesday, and this is not the cut to two sets you turned down on 3 August: Legs A asks for four calf sets and you have done two, two and three, and the weight only moves when you finish every set the plan asks for, so this makes the plan say three, which is what you actually do.

overrides.reason: Back to four sets — Tuesday's card cut this to three because it would have been your sixth day in a row, and you have taken two rest days since. The 120 and 140 are raises: you finished ten reps on 115, 135 and 145 last time, so those openers had gone stale. 145 stays where it is so the tenth rep at 150 is still there for you.
You took 120 for a clean ten on all three sets last Pull B, the top of the range every time, and 120 has been your ceiling here since 13 July. 127.5 is the smallest step this machine has.

Two nights at 37.5 and you have never cleared thirteen reps — the bottom of this range, not the top. The next pin is 45, and going lighter does not help either: 30 lb in July also gave you thirteen. Same weight, thirteen on all three sets.
The 70s went from 12, 12, 12 to 14, 13, 13 — moving the right way, but the rack jumps straight to 80 with nothing in between. Finish fifteen on all three sets and the 80s are yours.

Two sessions running you have been one rep short on the third set — 8, then 9. The next dumbbell is 30, a twenty percent jump bought with a set you have never finished. Two rest days is exactly the night that last rep lands.

At 37.5 your reps fell to 12, 11, 10 and the last two were under the twelve this slot asks for — that is the weight being wrong, not your effort. 35 is the nearest real step down on this stack, and the weight comes back once you are finishing fifteens there.
